facts.value: Town of Brookhaven Local Law No. 12 of 2026 enacts Chapter 17, Moratorium, and Article I, Data Centers Moratorium.
facts.supporting_quote: Local Law Enacting Chapter 17 of the Code of the Town of Brookhaven Entitled “Moratorium” and Creating a New Article I Entitled “Data Centers Moratorium”

facts.value: The cover letter is dated September 11, 2026, addressed to General Code Publishing Corp., and signed by Town Clerk Kevin J. LaValle. It states the law was adopted on August 13, 2026, but leaves the effective-date field blank.
facts.supporting_quote: Having been filed with the Secretary of State, this Local Law became effective .

facts.value: The New York Department of State, State Records Bureau, acknowledges that Local Law 12 of 2026 was filed on August 27, 2026; its Department of State index number is also 12 of 2026.
facts.supporting_quote: Local Law 12 of the year 2026 was filed with this office on 8/27/2026. The Department of State Local Law Index Number 12 of the year of 2026.

facts.value: The state acknowledgment letter is dated September 3, 2026; a separate receipt stamp bears September 11, 2026, at 9:10 a.m. Neither is the filing date stated in the letter.
facts.locator: Physical page 2, letter date and upper-right stamp

facts.value: The law's first page is marked A: 08/13/2026 and E: 08/27/2026.
The law provides for effectiveness immediately upon filing with the New York Secretary of State.
facts.supporting_quote: This local law shall become effective immediately upon filing with the Secretary of State of New York.

facts.value: The temporary moratorium is intended to pause data-center development while the town develops comprehensive zoning rules and assesses potential impacts; the law says it is not intended to prohibit data centers permanently.
facts.supporting_quote: The moratorium enables the Town to fully assess sites, needs, and develop land use regulations regarding the siting of such facilities

facts.value: The definition covers principal and accessory facilities and associated infrastructure primarily used for computer systems and digital services, including AI processing and cloud computing. Customary accessory server rooms, network closets and telecommunications rooms for on-site office-building operations are excluded.
facts.supporting_quote: Nothing herein shall be construed to include customary accessory server rooms or network closets, telecommunication rooms for on-site operations for office buildings.

facts.value: Section 17-3 bars review of new applications and the granting of applications, permits, licenses or approvals by town officers, departments, boards or agencies for specified data-center activities, from adoption until expiration. It does not expressly state a general prohibition on accepting applications.
facts.supporting_quote: No new applications shall be reviewed and no applications, permits, licenses or approvals shall be granted ... with respect to the erection, establishment, siting, location, construction, modification or development of any data centers ... from adoption of this chapter until the expiration of the term of this chapter.

facts.value: The land-use application prohibition does not apply to development pursuant to existing building permits or other application approvals, or to applications filed, duly accepted as complete and pending as of the chapter's effective date.
facts.supporting_quote: development pursuant to existing building permits or other application approvals and/or pursuant to applications which are filed, duly accepted as complete and pending, as of the effective date of this chapter

facts.value: A complete application must comply with Chapter 85, Planning Board regulations, and other applicable state and local laws, rules and regulations.
facts.supporting_quote: A complete application shall conform to and comply with all applicable requirements of Chapter 85 ... the Planning Board regulations ... and all other applicable state and local laws, rules and regulations.

facts.value: An affected property owner may apply in writing for relief with proof of unnecessary hardship. Mere delay in applying or waiting for a decision is not unnecessary hardship.
facts.supporting_quote: unnecessary hardship shall not be the mere delay in being permitted to make an application or waiting for a decision on the application

facts.value: The Town Board must find that hardship substantially exceeds any resulting public-welfare harm; the exemption will have no adverse effect on the town's planning or moratorium goals; and the project is compatible with community character and interim planning findings.
facts.supporting_quote: No relief shall be granted hereunder unless the Town Board shall specifically find and determine and shall set forth in its resolution granting such exemption

facts.value: After written application to the Town Clerk, the Board must schedule a public hearing within 30 days of receipt with five days' newspaper notice, decide within 30 days after the hearing closes, and grant only the minimum necessary relief if hardship is found.
facts.supporting_quote: within 30 days of receipt of said application, schedule a public hearing ... upon five days' written notice ... within 30 days of the close of said public hearing, render its decision

facts.value: The chapter states that it expires December 31, 2027.
facts.supporting_quote: This chapter shall expire on December 31, 2027.

facts.value: The chapter states an intent to supersede specified Town Law and locally incorporated time limits related to zoning and planning determinations.
facts.supporting_quote: supersede the provisions of the Town Law Chapter 16 ... relating to time limits in connection with zoning and planning determinations

uncertainties: The clerk's cover leaves its effective-date field blank; the separate state acknowledgment supplies the August 27 filing date, and the law's first page carries an E: 08/27/2026 notation.

Section 17-3 describes the restriction as running from adoption, while section 4 provides for effectiveness immediately upon filing and the exception uses the effective date. The document contains both formulations.
The trailing office abbreviation on the page 2 receipt stamp is faint; the date and time are distinguishable.
